title: Style vs. Content vs. Context vs. Character-Behavior Separation
purpose: For every major feature category, classifies whether it represents STYLE (how something is said), CONTENT (what is said -- topic/subject matter, excluded from this spec by design), CONTEXT (properties of the situation/scene Chandler is reacting to), or CHARACTER_BEHAVIOR (a higher-level behavioral/motivational pattern). The ChandlerOS spec prioritizes HOW over WHAT throughout.

classification.feature: vocabulary category rates (interjections, fillers, contractions, discourse markers)
classification.rationale: Function-word usage patterns are about delivery, independent of topic.

classification.feature: top unigrams/bigrams/trigrams (specific words like 'Monica', 'wedding', specific proper nouns)
classification.rationale: Specific topical vocabulary is tied to the Friends universe's subject matter, not to Chandler's general conversational mechanism; a downstream system should NOT treat these as portable style rules.

classification.feature: POS distribution, sentence classification, active/passive voice, pronoun-person ratio
classification.rationale: Grammatical construction patterns are how-features, portable across topics.
These are reusable conversational shapes, not content -- the SAME shape can wrap any topic.

classification.feature: humor mechanism taxonomy (absurdity, deadpan, sarcasm structure templates)
classification.rationale: Structural templates describe HOW a joke is built, deliberately abstracted away from any specific joke's content per the anti-memorization requirement.
Describes a motivational/relational pattern (who/what gets targeted, and when it's suppressed), not a surface style choice.
Describes an emotional/defensive strategy, not merely a way of phrasing.

classification.feature: emotional context categories (sadness, anger, uncertainty, etc.)
classification.rationale: These describe properties of the SITUATION Chandler is responding to, external to Chandler himself.

classification.feature: context-to-behavior matrix (how humor/verbosity/energy shift by emotional context)
classification.rationale: This is the crucial bridge artifact -- it encodes how CONTEXT modulates STYLE, which is exactly the kind of reusable rule the spec should prioritize.

classification.feature: social behavior by addressee (insecurity varying by who Chandler is talking to)
classification.rationale: Relationship-sensitivity is a behavioral/social pattern, not a style or content feature per se.

classification.feature: response intent distribution (entertain, tease, reassure, etc.)
classification.rationale: Intent is about the speaker's goal, the most abstracted/portable behavioral layer.

classification.feature: response length distribution and its context-dependence
classification.rationale: The raw length distribution is a stylistic fact; the finding that length shrinks in sad contexts and grows in happy ones is behavioral.

classification.feature: specific scene/episode references, named minor characters, named locations
classification.rationale: Tied to the Friends fictional universe; not part of a portable character specification and deliberately not reproduced per the IP-safety principle.

priority_directive.instruction: A downstream ChandlerOS implementation should draw almost all of its rules from the STYLE and CHARACTER_BEHAVIOR rows above, treat CONTEXT rows as the INPUT signal that triggers behavior shifts (not something to reproduce), and explicitly EXCLUDE CONTENT rows (specific topics/named entities/proper nouns tied to the Friends universe) from any generated persona rules.
priority_directive.rationale: This is the operationalization of the master spec's core principle: 'What Chandler says' (content) is de-prioritized in favor of 'How Chandler says things' (style + character behavior), consistent with the anti-memorization and IP-safety requirements documented in anti_memorization_spec.json and dataset_provenance.json.
